newsitem.title: JAPAN: Gap says expects 1997 revenues to top $6 bln.
newsitem.headline: Gap says expects 1997 revenues to top $6 bln.

text.p: Revenues of Gap Inc of the United States should exceed $6 billion in the 1997 business year, the head of its international unit said on Wednesday.
"Revenues this year are expected to top $6 billion," Gap International president William Fisher said at a seminar in Tokyo.
Gap said in May that its total sales for the first quarter of the 1997 business year were $1.23 billion.
The company, which owns the Gap, Banana Republic and Old Navy brands, plans to add almost 300 stores this year, 30 of them outside the United States, Fisher said.
Internationally, he said Gap plans to focus on countries in which it already has stores -- Japan, Canada, France, Germany and Britain.

Gap, which opened its flagship Japanese store in Tokyo in November 1996, also plans to enter markets such as Australia, Guam, Hong Kong, New Zealand and Singapore, Fisher said. He did not say when stores would be opened in those countries.
